new_assertions.body: The 5x3 post-T2 parity collision is a scheduler-phase alias in the tested carrier rather than evidence that the paired component types must be assigned arbitrary patched values: exact rank separates it, and rank mod 3 suffices in the tested corpus.

Multiplicity modulo m carries a homomorphic global phase projection because component types encode local support heights: total rank modulo m is the weighted sum of component counts modulo m. MOD3 success therefore cannot be read as a ternary component algebra without factoring this phase out.
The T2 W/L2/O reducer is recognizable from current-rank singleton residuals and the legal support frontier; ordinary child-state exploration is not required for its structural meaning.

The bounded key (component multiplicity parity, rank mod 3, T2) is Q-V exact on eight complete carriers but is not generally Q-F exact; it is therefore a scalar-value candidate, not a future-behavior quotient.

Within the tested cross-case candidates, rank mod 3 is a smaller sufficient phase than exact rank for the contextual Q-V key, while rank mod 4 is falsified on 5x3 and rank without T2 is falsified on every carrier.
A late exponent-2 quotient has reappeared only after scheduler/tactical phase factorization; this does not yet supply a component valuation phi, an XOR evaluator, or a universal group law.
